D15·0hh9 — 2026-08-05
chose: D14, three parts (user request): (a) `sofar statusline --install` — a one-command project-level installer that merges ONLY the statusLine key into <root>/.claude/settings.json, no hooks and no .sofar/, reusing init's merge law (existing statusLine always wins) and reporting wired/already/kept; (b) the identity segments quote Claude Code's default palette — dir YELLOW, branch BLUE — via a new non-semantic `Style.blue` reserved for exactly this and documented as unusable for state; (c) the model label drops `context` from a parenthesised window size, so "Opus 5 (1M context)" renders "Opus 5 (1M)". Model family tones are unchanged.
over: Telling users to hand-edit settings.json (the status quo — not shippable to anyone else); making them run `sofar init --statusline` and accept five hooks plus a .sofar/ they never asked for; keeping the D1 semantic palette on dir/branch (green branch) and accepting that the line looks unlike the one it replaces; and inventing a semantic meaning for blue to keep the law formally intact
because: The line is read-side and already degrades to model/dir/branch/ctx/cache with no record present, so wanting the line was never the same as wanting the tracking — tying them together was an artifact of --statusline being an init flag, not a design. On color: D6 established that the rent-meter REPLACES Claude's default line and must not cost the user what it replaced, and that argument covers appearance as much as content — a reproduction that recolors its source is not a reproduction. Calling blue a quotation rather than a meaning keeps D1 honest: the law binds color to meaning, and the one member that carries no meaning is marked as such instead of being given a fake one. Dropping `context` is the same word-over-glyph economy as D10/D11 — on a line that already reports ctx fill, the noun is the one part nobody has to read.
